![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/9f4f24dd100758466d8a06eee113bada8b1bede4b48c0a3e694e4c1e3f1c2371.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $z,$ then over a region $D$ in the $xy$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.
worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(y,z)$ and ${u}_{2}(y,z)$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z]\text{d}A.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 4,\,\,0\le z\le 1-\frac{x}{4},\,\,0\le y\le 1-\frac{x}{4}-z}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}A,$ we write $R$ as a type I region. 

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $z$-axis and in the direction of increasing $z,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/dc1a9b6371456f635cd4b73fe99301fa349ceeec1341b9bd3b86f6bcd7ad8ba2.png)

The arrow enters the region through the bottom boundary and leaves through the top boundary:

- The top boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(x,y),$ is

$$
y=1-\frac{x}{4}-z\,⟹\,z=1-\frac{x}{4}-y.
$$

- The bottom boundary of the region is

$$
z=0.
$$

Therefore, the type I representation of $R$ is 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,0\le z\le 1-\frac{x}{4}-y},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/07c4ee04dfba186348b3bd56b182477cec9ca1a581e37bb0eb4ab9a3d64ee515.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $z$ and then over $D,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4-y}f(x,y,z)\,dz]dA.\end{aligned}
$$
